input: Set up a pen pal exchange with overseas friends

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether this is physical letter writing, email, postcards, or a mix completely changes the setup steps, materials needed, and ongoing logistics.
Knowing how many friends are involved and whether they already know each other affects how the exchange is structured — one-to-one pairs vs. a group chain.
The countries involved determine postage costs, delivery times, customs rules for packages, and language considerations.
A budget for stamps, stationery, or care packages sets hard limits on what format and frequency are sustainable.
Whether the tone is casual and personal or themed/structured (e.g. sharing local culture, language learning) shapes what each exchange should contain and how prompts or templates should be designed.
The desired frequency of exchange (weekly, monthly, etc.) determines how much planning and scheduling infrastructure is needed to keep everyone on track.
Knowing what a successful exchange looks like — e.g. everyone responds consistently, friendships deepen, a cultural goal is met — determines which systems and check-ins to build in.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a pen pal exchange with overseas friends
gold.taskDescription: Organise a structured letter or message exchange with friends who live abroad.

questions.title: Physical letters, emails, or postcards — which format?
questions.description: Identify whether the exchange will use physical mail, digital messages, postcards, care packages, or a combination, as this determines all setup steps and materials.

questions.title: How many friends, and do they know each other?
questions.description: Clarify the number of participants and their relationships to determine if this is a series of one-to-one pairs or a group chain exchange.

questions.title: Which countries are your overseas friends based in?
questions.description: Knowing the destinations informs postage costs, delivery timelines, customs restrictions, and any language considerations.

questions.title: Is there a budget for postage or stationery?
questions.description: A spending limit shapes what formats and frequencies are realistically sustainable for all participants.

questions.title: Should exchanges be free-form or follow a theme?
questions.description: Decide whether letters are open and personal or built around recurring themes such as local culture, language learning, or seasonal events.

questions.title: How often should each exchange happen?
questions.description: Agree on a cadence — weekly, monthly, quarterly — so the right scheduling and reminder system can be put in place.

questions.title: What would make this exchange feel like a success?
questions.description: Define the end goal — consistent replies, deeper friendships, cultural learning, a completed scrapbook — to determine which tracking or check-in systems to build in.
